text:
samir: FYI I just noticed a p99 spike on the 8xA100 pool after yesterday's kernel swap. p95 is fine but p99 jumped ~420ms -> ~1.2s for some workloads.

liz: ugh, reproducible in perf tests? which workload?

samir: repros on long-context chat loads (avg seq_len ~1500, some max_tokens=2048). Profiling shows a lot of stall time in KV eviction + kernel fallback. snippet from perf tool: 
```
timeline: 
  decode: 120ms
  kv-evict-wait: 760ms  <-- suspicious
  kernel-fallback: 230ms
  total: 1.11s
```

jess: KV eviction waits that high usually mean the cache thrashing with large prefixes and microbatch reorder. Did we change batching heuristics?

samir: We flipped kernel selection to prefer fused-attn for medium seqs, but it falls back to generic kernel when KV allocation fails. That fallback path is heavier. Also microbatch size bumped to 32 for throughput experiments on that pool.

kai: So tradeoff between throughput and tail latency. If microbatch=32 we get better throughput but more overlapping KV state and evictions.

liz: Could we try an adaptive truncation policy: dynamically clamp effective max_tokens based on queue depth and recent p99? e.g., when queue depth > threshold, apply soft cap: max_tokens_effective = min(requested, 1024 + 256 * load_factor)

jess: I like soft caps instead of hard rejections. Also we should add a short timeout/circuit-breaker for kernel-fallback path: if fallback kernel latency > X for N requests, route to smaller microbatch or drop back to previous kernel.

samir: I ran an experiment locally: when I force a truncation to 1024 for high-load traces, p99 drops to ~520ms and throughput only loses ~8%. Command I used to replay: `./perf-replay --trace traceA.json --apply-truncation=1024 --microbatch=16`

deploy-bot: CI perf job #5423 finished: baseline vs candidate shows p99 -48% on traceA when truncation=1024 + microbatch=16. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/5423

kai: nice. We should also tweak KV cache eviction policy: prefer LRU with prefix-awareness so we avoid evicting recent high-hit prefixes. That will reduce eviction stalls.

liz: Agree. Action items: 1) try adaptive soft-cap on max_tokens in runtime (samir + jess) 2) experiment microbatch=16 on pool during peak windows (kai) 3) add fallback circuit breaker to kernel selection path (jess) 4) KV eviction tune + prefix-awareness (samir).

samir: I'll open a PR with adaptive cap flag and a runtime knob: `--soft-max-tokens-threshold=1200` and a new metric `runtime.soft_truncate.count`.

jess: I'll prototype the kernel-fallback circuit as an exponential backoff: if fallback p99 > 300ms for 30s, force kernel_preference=stable for that slot.

liz: also add an observability dashboard: p50/p95/p99, kv-evict-wait histogram, kernel-fallback-rate, soft-truncate-rate. Want that before we flip pool.

kai: I'll schedule a canary with microbatch=16 + soft-cap=1024 for the 8xA100 pool tomorrow 03:00 UTC and monitor for 2 hours.

samir: thanks. One more note — we should avoid aggressive global `max_tokens` enforcement for enterprise customers (they expect exact outputs). Make soft-cap opt-out per-tenant and default on shared pools.

liz: agreed. Let's sync after the canary and roll the changes slowly. :thumbsup:
